key_insight: Stronger stable stratification weakens Lagrangian power fluctuations yet increases their negative skewness, revealing greater temporal asymmetry in particle-level kinetic-energy exchange.
engineering_relevance: These results can inform assessment of turbulence models for stratified flows by highlighting topology-dependent and directional differences in energy exchange.
method: Direct numerical simulations of homogeneous Boussinesq turbulence.
Three nonzero stratification strengths compared with an unstratified reference.
Topology-conditioned power, pressure redistribution, and tracer persistence statistics.
evidence_signal: Simulations show decreasing global power variance, increasingly negative standardized skewness, and exponential tracer-persistence tails with topology-dependent time scales.
watch_item: The causal links among power asymmetry, pressure-mediated redistribution, and altered tracer sampling remain unestablished.
